key_insight: The simulations predict that calcium channel blockers reduce arterial media stress but shift load to the fibrous cap, potentially increasing plaque rupture risk if blood pressure reduction is insufficient.
engineering_relevance: Coupled drug-transport and arterial-mechanics modeling reveals local stress trade-offs that should be considered when assessing treatment effects on atherosclerotic plaques.
method: Couple 3D reaction–diffusion drug transport with finite element arterial mechanics.
Model calcium-dependent smooth muscle contraction and drug–tissue interactions.
Include nonlinear anisotropic tissue behavior and residual stresses.
evidence_signal: With material parameters fitted to literature experiments, simulations of five histology-derived geometries predicted fibrous-cap stress increases in all five, with median increases up to 28.9 kPa; a 10 mmHg blood pressure reduction limited median increases to at most 3.8 kPa in four geometries.
watch_item: The predicted increase in plaque rupture risk remains unconfirmed experimentally and clinically, and evaluation covered only five exemplary geometries.
paper_title: Pharmaco-mechanical computational simulation of atherosclerotic arteries: effects of calcium channel blockers on local stress distributions
